raw.query: WITH relevant AS (SELECT p.run_id, p.window_name, p.lead_s, p.p99_ms, p.n_requests, p.queue_divergent, p.is_current, d.superseded_by FROM provenance.v_pool_latency p JOIN provenance.v_dim d USING (run_id) WHERE p.is_current = true AND d.is_current = true AND p.policy = 'reactive' AND p.sla_metric = 'encoder_delay' AND p.window_name IN ('burst1','steady24h') AND p.lead_s IS NOT NULL) SELECT window_name, lead_s, COUNT(*) AS current_rows, MIN(p99_ms) AS min_p99_ms, MAX(p99_ms) AS max_p99_ms, MIN(n_requests) AS min_requests, MAX(n_requests) AS max_requests, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE p99_ms >= 1000) AS sla_violations, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE queue_divergent) AS divergent_rows, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE superseded_by IS NOT NULL) AS superseded_rows FROM relevant GROUP BY window_name, lead_s ORDER BY window_name, lead_s
raw.observed: At every current tested window-lead cell, reactive encoder-delay p99 is below 1000 ms: burst1 maxima are 588.37, 742.829, 588.37, 609.707, and 904.739 ms at leads 15, 30, 45, 165, and 300 s; steady24h values are 548.363, 682.109, 733.643, and 733.643 ms at leads 15, 30, 45, and 165 s. Every cell has 0 SLA violations, 0 divergent rows, and 0 superseded rows.
raw.claimed: Slow ramps (burst1, the calm day) are reactive-scalable at any tested lead
raw.evidence: In the enclosing encoder-pool scope, all current reactive runs for burst1 and steady24h satisfy the 1000 ms encoder-delay p99 SLA at every lead represented in v_pool_latency.
